1.note: See how you translated the expression “burden” in [13:1](ta:13). Alternate translation: [A message about]

Isaiah is speaking to the **ships of Tarshish** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the destruction of Tyre, a busy port they use frequently. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the ships of Tarshish. Alternate translation: [Wail for the ships of Tarshish]

The expression **it has been destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [their enemy has destroyed it]
The pronoun **it** refers to the city of Tyre. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Tyre has been destroyed]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [so that no house remains and a ship cannot safely enter the harbor]

The expression **it was revealed to them** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the sailors of Tarshish learned about it]

2.note: Isaiah is speaking to the **dwellers of the coastland** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the destruction of Tyre. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the dwellers of the coastland. Alternate translation: [Let the dwellers of the coastland be silent]

The word **you** is feminine singular because it refers to the city of Tyre, which is being personified as a woman. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction, and use the feminine form if your language marks that distinction.

3.note: Isaiah is using this possessive form to mean “the grain grown at Shihor.” It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the grain that grows near Shihor]
The pronouns **its** and **it** refer to the city of Tyre. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [was revenue for Tyre, and Tyre became]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **revenue**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [was what made it wealthy]

4.note: Isaiah is speaking to the city of **Sidon** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the fall of its ally Tyre. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about Sidon. Alternate translation: [The people of Sidon should feel shame]

Isaiah is speaking of **the sea** as if it were a person who could speak. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Tyre, the stronghold of the sea, has spoken, saying]

4.q: לֹֽא חַ֣לְתִּי וְ⁠לֹֽא יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְ⁠לֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת
4.note: Isaiah is speaking of **the sea** as if it were a mother who could bear and raise children. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have no people; there are no young men or young women among me]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I have not brought up virgins]

Isaiah is referring to all of the young people by naming two major components, **young men** and **virgins**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I have not raised up any young people, whether young men or young women]

5.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of a **report**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what was heard]
The pronoun **they** refers to the Egyptians. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the Egyptians will writhe]

Here Isaiah is speaking as if the Egyptians’ distress were the pains of labor, causing them to **writhe**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the Egyptians will be in great anguish]

6.note: Isaiah is speaking to the **dwellers of the coastland** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the destruction of Tyre. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the dwellers of the coastland. Alternate translation: [Cross over toward Tarshish; the dwellers of the coastland must wail]

7.q: הֲ⁠זֹ֥את לָ⁠כֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽ⁠ימֵי קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָ⁠הּ֙
7.note: Isaiah is using the question form to express disbelief that this once-exultant city has fallen. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is hard to believe that this is the exultant one to you, its origin from days of antiquity!]
Isaiah is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from ancient times]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **antiquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [very long ago]

Isaiah is speaking of the city of Tyre as if it were a person whose **feet** could carry it to distant places. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Its residents traveled far away to live in distant lands]

8.q: מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל צֹ֖ר הַ⁠מַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֨י⁠ה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖י⁠הָ נִכְבַּדֵּי אָֽרֶץ
8.note: Isaiah is using the question form to emphasize that it was Yahweh who determined this destruction against Tyre. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh determined this against Tyre, the one crowning, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were honored ones of the earth.]

Here Isaiah is speaking as if Tyre were a king **crowning** other rulers. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one who appointed rulers]

Here Isaiah is speaking as if the merchants of Tyre were **princes**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [whose merchants had great authority]

Isaiah is using the adjective **honored** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [were highly respected people of the earth]

9.note: Here, **to** marks **to profane the pride of all of the splendor** as the goal or purpose of what **Yahweh of Armies determined**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [for his purpose of profaning the pride of all of the splendor]

Here, **to** marks **to make light all of the honored ones of the earth** as a second goal or purpose of what **Yahweh of Armies determined**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [and for making light all of the honored ones of the earth]

See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of clauses in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [to bring disgrace on all who were glorious and honored on the earth]

Isaiah is speaking as if the pride of Tyre were a sacred object that Yahweh would **profane**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to dishonor all of their great pride]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **pride** and **splendor**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [all that it gloried in and was proud of]

The expression **honored ones** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom the earth honored]

Isaiah is using the adjective **honored** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the people who were held in honor on the earth]

10.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the Nile** overflows freely across the land, so the people of Tarshish should now spread out freely over their land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as the Nile overflows freely across the land]

Here Isaiah is speaking as if the people of Tarshish were a **daughter**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people who live in Tarshish]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **restraint**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [holding them back]

11.note: Here, **his hand** represents Yahweh’s power and authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [his mighty hand]

Isaiah is using **kingdoms** to represent the people of those kingdoms. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he made the people of kingdoms tremble]

The term that the ULT translates as **merchant** originally meant “Canaan.” That name came to mean “merchant” because Canaanites, especially Phoenicians such as the ones in Tyre, were traders. Some interpreters believe that the name is intended here. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.
The pronoun **its** refers to the merchant city of Tyre. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Tyre’s strongholds]

12.note: Yahweh is using **You will not add again** as a common expression to mean “you will no longer” rejoice. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You will no longer rejoice]

The expression **oppressed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [virgin of the daughter of Sidon whom others have oppressed]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **daughter of Sidon** who is characterized by being a **virgin**, an unmarried young woman. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [virgin daughter of Sidon]

Yahweh is addressing a representative young female resident of the city of Sidon as if she were the **daughter** of that city. (In this culture, it was such women who publicly celebrated the victories of their cities.) If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you young woman who lives in Sidon]

The word “you” in both instances and the implied “you” in the imperatives **Arise** and **cross over** are feminine singular because Yahweh is addressing one representative woman. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction, and use the feminine form if your language marks that distinction.

13.note: Isaiah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look]

Isaiah is using **This people is not** as a common expression to mean “This people has ceased to exist as a nation.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [This people no longer exists as a nation]
The pronoun **one** does not refer to a specific person but is used in a general sense. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [they made it a ruin]

14.note: Isaiah is again speaking to the **ships of Tarshish** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the destruction of Tyre. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the ships of Tarshish. See how you translated the similar expression in [23:1](ta:23). Alternate translation: [Wail for the ships of Tarshish]

The expression **has been destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [enemies have destroyed your stronghold]

15.note: Isaiah is using the phrase translated as **And it will happen** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
Isaiah is using the term **day** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at that time]

The expression **will be forgotten** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that people will forget Tyre]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the days of one king** last about 70 years, so Tyre will be forgotten for 70 years. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [about as long as a typical king’s life lasts]

The point of this comparison is that just as the **song of the prostitute** tries to win back former clients, so Tyre will try to regain its former trade. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like the song sung about a prostitute trying to win back her former clients]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **song** that is sung by a **prostitute**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [like the song sung about a prostitute] or [like a song that a prostitute sings]

16.note: The expression **forgotten** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [prostitute whom people forgot]

The expression **be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so that people may recall you]

17.note: Isaiah is using the phrase translated as **And it will happen** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

17.q: וְ⁠שָׁבָ֖ה לְ⁠אֶתְנַנָּ֑⁠ה וְ⁠זָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת כָּל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ
17.note: Here Isaiah is speaking as if Tyre’s trading activity were the act of a prostitute who would **whore** with the kingdoms. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And she will return to her trading profit, and she will trade with all of the kingdoms of the earth]

Isaiah says **all of the kingdoms of the earth** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [every kingdom on earth]

Isaiah is using **the face of the ground** as a common expression to mean “the surface of the earth.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everywhere]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **hire**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to earning money]

18.note: Here Isaiah is speaking as if Tyre’s trading **profit** and **hire** were the wages of a prostitute. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [her trading profits]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [holy]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **profit** and **hire**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [all she earns and receives as wages]

The expression **It will not be stored** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [They will not store it]

The expression **it will not be hoarded** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will hoard it]

Here, **the face of Yahweh** represents being in the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **satiety**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [enough to be full]
